# Data files

All files in this folder are **synthetic**. They were produced by random generators in
`scripts/` and do not describe real students of MIT-ADT University or any other institution.
They exist so the application and the machine-learning pipeline can be demonstrated end to end.

## training_data.csv  (generated by `scripts/generate_training_data.py`)

1500 labelled rows used to train and evaluate the risk classifier.

| Column | Type | Used as model input? | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| attendance_pct | 0–100 | yes | Attendance percentage |
| previous_gpa | 0–10 (4 % missing) | yes | Previous semester GPA / SGPA |
| quiz_score | 0–100 | yes | Average quiz score |
| test_score | 0–100 (3 % missing) | yes | Average internal test score |
| assignment_completion_pct | 0–100 | yes | Share of assignments submitted |
| study_hours | 0–9 (5 % missing) | yes | Average daily self-study hours |
| participation | Low / Medium / High | yes | Class participation rating |
| engagement_level | Low / Medium / High | yes | Engagement rating |
| self_understanding | 1–5 | yes | Self-reported understanding of concepts |
| quiz_trend | points (15 % missing) | yes | Change in recent assessment scores (later half − earlier half) |
| final_exam_pct | 0–100 | **no (leakage)** | Simulated final exam result, known only after the semester |
| risk_label | Low / Medium / High | **target** | Derived from final_exam_pct |

**Target definition:** `High` if final_exam_pct < 40 (fail), `Medium` if 40 ≤ final_exam_pct < 55
(borderline pass), `Low` if ≥ 55. The exam result and the label are never used as inputs.

**Generation process (summary):** a latent "academic standing" variable and a correlated "effort"
variable drive every indicator with independent Gaussian noise; the final exam result depends on
those indicators plus substantial unexplained variation (σ ≈ 9 points), so no single input
determines the label and the achievable accuracy is deliberately well below 100 %.

To supply real data, keep the same column names (either `risk_label` or `final_exam_pct` must be
present) and retrain with `python scripts/train_model.py --data path/to/file.csv`.

## sample_students.csv and sample_assessments.csv  (generated by `scripts/make_sample_data.py`)

45 fictional students across three classes and 156 historical quiz/test scores, in the exact
format accepted by the CSV import page and `scripts/seed_demo.py`. Names are random combinations
of common Indian first and last names and correspond to no real person.
